type: fleet carrier (converted battlecruiser hull; single flight deck after the 1935-38 rebuild)
schema_notes: level_m = deck height above the waterline. confidence: sourced / typical / reconstruction.

basis.fact: After the 1938 rebuild: length 260.67 m, beam 31.32 m, draught 8.71 m; 36,500 long tons standard, 41,300 deep load
Rebuild gave one flight deck ~249 m long over two enclosed hangars
Island on the port side (Kaga's on the starboard); funnels on the starboard side, angled downward, below the flight deck
Hangar area after rebuild 6,521.1 m2; aircraft 60 -> 91; flight deck made single and continuous on 31 Aug 1938
Originally completed with three stepped flight decks and twin 20 cm turrets on the middle level
Flagship of the First Air Fleet, Apr 1941; sailed for Pearl Harbor from Hitokappu Bay 26 Nov 1941
Midway: Lt Richard Best's bomb hit at the aft edge of the middle elevator and exploded in the upper hangar among fuelled, armed B5N torpedo bombers
Yamamoto ordered her scuttled; destroyers Arashi, Hagikaze, Maikaze, Nowaki torpedoed her on 5 June 1942
Wreck found Oct 2019 by RV Petrel at ~5,490 m

flooding.watertight_subdivision: Battlecruiser hull with armoured belt and transverse bulkheads below the main deck; the enclosed hangars above are essentially open fire zones with poor ventilation for venting explosions.
flooding.pumps: Fire mains; electric pumps failed when power was lost (typical)
flooding.sea_cocks: Kingston valves (typical); magazines had flooding valves

sequence: ~10:26 one 1,000 lb bomb at the aft edge of the middle elevator, exploding in the upper hangar
A near miss jams the rudder
Fuelled, armed aircraft and ordnance in the hangar explode; fire spreads through both hangars
Bridge abandoned; Nagumo transfers to cruiser Nagara
Ship burns all night, dead in the water but afloat (hull intact below the waterline)
5 June: scuttled by destroyer torpedoes; sinks bow first

game_sinking_hooks: Fire spreading between hangar bays: ordnance on trolleys causes chain explosions
The hull stays afloat despite total burnout; sinking requires torpedoes/scuttling (open sea cocks)
Fire curtains can slow the spread
